obtained.how: publisher's own open web page: Atlantic Salmon Federation, 'ASF Rivernotes 3 Sept. 2021' (the ?p=36632 link redirects to it)

bibliography.checked_against: the web page (title, date and byline)
bibliography.note: 'ASF Rivernotes 3 Sept. 2021', 'September 3, 2021', 'Compiled by Tom Moffatt'; the Maine item is headed 'New focus on Maine rivers east of Mt. Katahdin' — matches the entry

claims.claim: the Atlantic Salmon Federation places Danforth about 130 mi (≈ 209 km) above tidewater
claims.location: web page, Maine headwaters item ('New focus on Maine rivers east of Mt. Katahdin')
claims.quote: Veazie Dam that the Penobscot Project removed, and 130 miles above tidewater
claims.conditions: said of 'this part of the Penobscot watershed' — the Crooked Brook / Baskahegan Lake fishway site, 'adjacent to Danforth'; a round figure in a newsletter, method not given; 130 mi × 1.609 = 209 km
claims.note: the item also puts the site 100 miles above the former Veazie Dam. It is the fishway site at the Baskahegan Lake outlet, not Hot Brook's mouth; the paper's own NHDPlus 203.5 km is the better number and is consistent

claims.claim: sea-run alewives reached Danforth by natural straying, confirmed by Maine DMR in 2017, 'the farthest inland known to recolonize naturally on the East Coast' (cited 'ASF 2021, 2024')
claims.note: not in ASF 2021: the item never says alewives had already reached Danforth, names no DMR confirmation, and has no such quotation (searched 'inland', 'natural', 'DMR', 'recoloni', 'East Coast'). Its only 2017 is a local committee working on the project 'since 2017'. The straying, the DMR 2017 confirmation and the quotation belong to ASF 2024 (per the project's notes, ASF 31 Jul 2024) — cite that alone

claims.claim: a fishway for river herring on Baskahegan Stream at Danforth
claims.quote: a new $198,000 project to install a fishway for river herring at Baskahegan Lake
claims.conditions: September 2021: a planned project, 'at Baskahegan Lake and Crooked Brook' ('The dam on Crooked Brook will be reworked to provide fish passage upstream to Baskahegan'); the photo caption names it the 'Crooked Brook and Baskahegan Stream Fish Passage Project'
claims.note: ASF 2021 supports only the project's existence and purpose; 'built in 2023' needs ASF 2024

notes: Cite ASF 2021 for the 130-mi figure and the planned fishway only; move the natural-straying, DMR-2017 and 'farthest inland' statements to ASF 2024. Other content: the item frames river herring as prey cover for outmigrating salmon smolts and says headwater passage is 'imperative because that is where spawning takes place'; the Mattawamkeag branch is 'the extensive easternmost branch of the Penobscot River watershed'; the site is 'just a few miles from the adjacent St. Croix watershed and East Grand Lake'.
